premises.text: Employers drown in irrelevant applications on Craigslist/Monster/CareerBuilder while job seekers cannot get noticed or know if applications were viewed
premises.evidence_span: That system is broken. Let's have a look on the other side of the coin for the job seekers

premises.text: LocalBacon offers dynamic job search with save, uniform handpicked full-time quality listings (no MLM/scams)
premises.evidence_span: we handpick every single job that's posted on our site. That means that they're all full-time opportunities

premises.text: Job seekers pay to apply via discounted job credits starting at $0.99, which employers notice; employers agree to feedback and view notifications
premises.evidence_span: job seekers pay to apply on LocalBacon. And they notice that

premises.text: Application center with in-site iPaper resume viewing and employer triage (new/flagged/shelved) plus ATS handoff and candidate transparency emails
premises.evidence_span: This lands the job in our application center. This is mission control for a job seeker

value.text: Fix fundamental hiring problems for both job seekers and employers—signal quality candidates and reduce noise
value.evidence_span: we created LocalBacon to fix the fundamental problems that exist for both job seekers and employers

causal_links.evidence_span: Monster, CareerBuilder, and Craigslist, they're broken
Job seekers want to get noticed. On our website, the employers and recruiters that we work with know that job seekers pay to apply
as an employer, I gain credibility for giving transparency to my process without changing my behavior

notes: Employer noise + seeker invisibility folded as one two-sided hiring pain (§4.1.6).
